title: Anisotropic Brushed Metal with Direction Control & Save/Load
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that demonstrates an interactive anisotropic brushed metal material with direction control and save/load state functionality.

## Scene Setup
- Black background (0x111111).
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 0, 4), FOV 50.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation (damping enabled).
- Lighting: one DirectionalLight (white, intensity 1.5) at (5, 5, 5), one DirectionalLight (white, intensity 0.8) at (-3, 2, -2), one AmbientLight (0x333333).
- An environment map using THREE.PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural equirectangular scene (use a small RGBELoader-free approach: create a small DataTexture with gradient colors simulating an HDR studio, or use Scene-based env with colored meshes). The env map must be assigned to the material.

## Primary Object
- A single THREE.Mesh: a TorusKnot geometry (radius 1.0, tube 0.35, tubularSegments 128, radialSegments 32, p=2, q=3).
- Use THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial with these initial properties:
  - color: 0xbbbbbb (silver)
  - metalness: 1.0
  - roughness: 0.35
  - anisotropy: 0.7 (THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial supports anisotropy in r162+)
  - anisotropyRotation: 0.0 (radians)
  - clearcoat: 0.1
  - clearcoatRoughness: 0.2
- The object rotates slowly on Y axis (0.003 rad/frame). Rotation can be toggled.

## Anisotropy Direction Control
- A circular on-screen direction widget (canvas-based HUD, 100x100px, bottom-left corner, 20px margin).
- The widget shows a circle with a line from center indicating the current anisotropy direction angle.
- Clicking/dragging on the widget sets the anisotropy rotation angle (atan2 of click relative to center). Update material.anisotropyRotation in real time.
- Alternatively, pressing A/D keys rotates the anisotropy direction by ±0.05 radians per press.

## HUD Controls (DOM overlay, top-left, styled dark semi-transparent panel)
- Slider: 'Anisotropy Strength' (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01, default 0.7) → controls material.anisotropy
- Slider: 'Roughness' (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01, default 0.35) → controls material.roughness
- Slider: 'Metalness' (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01, default 1.0) → controls material.metalness
- Slider: 'Clearcoat' (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01, default 0.1) → controls material.clearcoat
- Color picker: 'Metal Color' (default #bbbbbb) → controls material.color
- Checkbox: 'Auto Rotate' (default checked) → toggles Y-axis auto-rotation
- Button: 'Save State' (id='saveBtn') → serializes current state to localStorage key 'brushedMetalState'
- Button: 'Load State' (id='loadBtn') → restores state from localStorage, updates all sliders/material/widget
- Button: 'Reset' (id='resetBtn') → resets all values to defaults
- Display label showing current anisotropy rotation in degrees (id='angleDisplay').

## Save/Load State Format
The saved state object must contain: { anisotropy, anisotropyRotation, roughness, metalness, clearcoat, colorHex, autoRotate, savedAt (ISO timestamp) }.

## State Management (CRITICAL)
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields, updated every frame in the animation loop:
- anisotropy: (number) current material.anisotropy
- anisotropyRotation: (number) current material.anisotropyRotation in radians
- anisotropyRotationDeg: (number) anisotropyRotation converted to degrees
- roughness: (number) current material.roughness
- metalness: (number) current material.metalness
- clearcoat: (number) current material.clearcoat
- colorHex: (string) current material color as hex string like '#bbbbbb'
- autoRotate: (boolean) whether auto-rotation is on
- objectRotationY: (number) current object rotation.y
- meshExists: (boolean) true if mesh is in scene
- materialType: (string) material.type e.g. 'MeshPhysicalMaterial'
- envMapAssigned: (boolean) material.envMap !== null
- savedStateExists: (boolean) localStorage.getItem('brushedMetalState') !== null
- lastSavedAt: (string|null) timestamp from last save, or null
- sliderAnisotropyValue: (number) parseFloat of the anisotropy slider DOM value
- sliderRoughnessValue: (number) parseFloat of the roughness slider DOM value
- frameCount: (number) incremented each animation frame
- isNaNFree: (boolean) true if none of anisotropy, anisotropyRotation, roughness, metalness, clearcoat are NaN
physics_constraints: All material parameters must remain within valid [0,1] bounds. AnisotropyRotation must be a finite number (no NaN/Infinity). Color must always be a valid hex. Save/load must be lossless — loaded state must exactly match saved state within floating point tolerance (epsilon < 0.001). Auto-rotation delta must be consistent (0.003 rad/frame when enabled, 0 when disabled).
